question: Tell me about a time two teams had goals that worked against each other. How did you resolve it?

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time two teams had goals that worked against each other. How did you resolve it?
On my project, the backend team wanted to ship a new API quickly while my frontend team needed stability for a demo. I flagged it in standup and asked my manager for help aligning priorities.
I met with the backend lead to share the demo deadline and we agreed to a small change that let both move forward. The demo went well and we learned to check dependencies earlier.

junior.raiseFeedback: Raises the bar for junior. Company-wide Perspective question. Candidate described noticing API vs demo conflict and escalating to manager before coordinating a small compromise with the other team. "I met with the backend lead to share the demo deadline and we agreed to a small change" shows ownership of their local scope and willingness to learn. This meets expectations at junior level where individual initiative and coachability matter more than cross-team strategy. Biggest strength is quick escalation combined with follow-through on the fix.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time two teams had goals that worked against each other. How did you resolve it?
Marketing wanted faster feature releases while Platform focused on stability SLOs. I pulled both leads into a review of release metrics and we created a joint process with staged rollouts.

I showed data on customer impact from both fast features and incidents, then proposed a pilot that reduced incidents 20% while keeping release cadence. Both teams adopted it and we tracked it for two quarters.

raiseTranscript.text: Tell me about a time two teams had goals that worked against each other. How did you resolve it?

Sales committed to custom features while Engineering was measured on platform reliability. I restructured incentives so both orgs shared a customer retention metric and created a joint roadmap review.
We accepted slower feature velocity for six months to stabilize the platform, which improved retention 15% and let us renegotiate sales targets. This became the model for other product areas.
